text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Prod routing spike: model-runner containers segfaulting -> elevated 5xx across inference-gateway (5xx rate 14%). Auto-page to oncall.
jamal: acked. I'm oncall, pulling logs now. tagging @alex for runtime eyeballs.
alex: looking. seeing repeated SIGSEGV in /opt/runner/lib/model_exec.so on hot path. repro on a single host so far.
jamal: which host? pod names?
alex: pod model-runner-5c8f9 / node gpu-17. CrashLoopBackOff after ~30s of serving long-context requests. snippet:
```
#0  0x7f4abcde in model_forward
#1  0x7f4abf12 in kv_cache_update
#2  0x7f4ac001 in attention_compute
SIGSEGV at 0x0
```
linda: pinging infra: any node OOMs or driver resets? @pagerduty
pagerduty: node gpu-17 shows dmesg GPU fault then container crash. No full node OOM. Driver reset logged at kernel: ttm_eviction: retry fail.
alex: looks like a GPU kernel crash triggers segfault in process userspace. Could be a bad kernel or recent model runner change. Was there a deploy? jamal, any traffic push around 1935004200?
jamal: we rolled model-runner:v2.4.1 ~5m ago during canary. Canary passed quick smoke, then traffic increased and failures started.
tara-cs: CS escalation — customers seeing inference 500s: AcmeCorp (high-traffic), MediData. Impact: blocking batch jobs for AcmeCorp, interactive latencies failing for ~12% of requests.
jamal: triage plan: 1) isolate failing host, 2) shift traffic off GPU-17, 3) rollback runner to v2.4.0 on affected pool, 4) create fallback routing to quantized-variant. Anyone object?
alex: +1. Also capture core dump and upload to S3 for later analysis. Run gcore before restarting.
linda: initiating traffic drain from node gpu-17 now: cordon + drain with graceful 30s. command:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-17
kubectl drain gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```
incident-bot: ACTION logged: cordon/drain started by linda.
alex: trying to gcore the crashing pid; if it dies too fast we'll enable core_pattern to pipe to file. running:
```
kubectl exec -it model-runner-5c8f9 -- gcore -o /tmp/core.$$ 1234 || echo failed
kubectl cp model-runner-5c8f9:/tmp/core.* s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1935004321/
```
jamal: rolling back runner to v2.4.0 on prod pool A now. patching deployment image and forcing restart.
linda: rollback pushed. pods creating, healthchecks passing for new pods. routing policy adjusted to avoid gpu-17 and to prefer pool-B.
pagerduty: traffic shift confirmed, 80% of requests moved off gpu-17 within 90s.
alex: monitoring logs — 5xx rate dropping from 14% -> 3% after rollback and drain. still seeing intermittent 500s for long-context requests; might be cached sessions hitting old nodes, or KV cache corruption.
tara-cs: customer impact update: AcmeCorp reported errors cleared for interactive flows but batch job replay will be needed. Notifying top 3 customers now. drafting statuspage update.
jamal: assigning owner for follow-up investigation: alex + eng-runtime. Runbooks: set failover policy to fully avoid single-node routing for long-seq models. Also add preflight kernel smoke on deploy to check for driver regressions.
alex: captured core and uploaded. file s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1935004321/model-runner-core-gpu-17.tar.gz. creating internal bug INC-2026-912 for segfault analysis.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-912 created and linked. Priority P1.
linda: oncall handoff in 30m to next rotation @linda -> @jamal? jamal: I'm staying to finish postmortem fragments, but handoff to second oncall (linda) for operational followups. marking in channel.
tara-cs: statuspage draft: "We are experiencing elevated 5xx errors for some inference requests due to an internal runtime crash in a model-runner process. We have mitigated by rolling back to a previous runner version and draining affected hosts. Some customers experienced transient errors; we are following up individually." Please review before publish.
jamal: published. Also notifying sales and support slack channels.
pagerduty: metrics: 5xx returned to baseline 0.6% within 12 minutes of mitigation. Logging ticked as mitigated by rollback+drain.
alex: next steps: reproduce with stress test on v2.4.1, bisect commit range, run GPU driver regression tests, add Canary traffic more slowly and gate long-context workloads behind additional checks. Postmortem owner: alex. ETA draft in 48h.
incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED -> monitoring for 1h. If regressions reappear, page oncall.
jamal: thanks all. closing communication loop with customers and ops. adding notes to the incident doc.
